# Code Theming Survey — Nexus (for the "elvish" third theme)

## 1. `apps/web/src/app/globals.css` (402 lines) — full token map

**L1**: `@import "./brand.css"` — auto-generated (`scripts/build-icons.mjs`, do not hand-edit) 4 tokens: `--brand-fg-on-dark`/`-on-light` (#c4a472 / #7d5e35) and `--brand-bg-dark`/`-on-light` (#15140f / #faf8f3), consumed by `--accent` (L159, L200) and by `layout.tsx`/`manifest.ts` for theme-color meta.

**L3–179 `:root`**: theme-invariant scale tokens (type scale L23–34, leading L36–41, tracking L43–48, weight L50–54, radius L56–63, spacing L70–84, motion easing/duration L86–94, control sizing L96–102, z-index L104–110, overlay scrims L112–114, layout geometry L116–130) — none of these need touching for a new theme. Also **highlight inks** L132–137 (`--highlight-yellow/green/blue/pink/purple`), explicitly commented "theme-invariant translucent fills" — confirmed independently by `lib/highlights/colors.ts` (below), which only maps color→label, no per-theme values.

Then **default (dark) semantic colors**, L139–178: `--surface-canvas/-1/-2/-3/-hover/-active/-sunken`, `--ink/-muted/-faint`, `--ink-machine` + `--rail-machine` (derived via `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink-machine) 34%, transparent)`, L154), `--ink-on-accent`, `--edge/-subtle/-strong`, `--accent` (aliases `--brand-fg-on-dark`), `--accent-hover/-active/-muted`, `--ring`, `--success/-warning/-danger/-info`, `--shadow-1..5`, and four "Two Rooms" room-specific knobs: `--stroke-hairline` (1.5px dark / 1px light), `--body-font-size` (`--text-md` dark / `--text-base` light — a deliberate optical-size swap, not just color), `--tracking-body` (0.008em dark / 0 light), `--canvas-grain-opacity`+`--canvas-grain-image` (grain only in dark "Press" room; light "Study" room is grain-free — L177–178 is an inline SVG feTurbulence data-URI).

**L182–220 `[data-theme="light"]`**: full override block, same token set, "Study" values (paper #faf8f3, ink #1a1a1c, accent aliases `--brand-fg-on-light` #7d5e35).

**L223–263 `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { :root:not([data-theme]) { ... } }`**: byte-for-byte duplicate of the light block, guarding the no-cookie "system" case. **Any new theme must NOT be reachable through this fallback** — it only ever resolves to light or the dark `:root` default; a 3rd value is only reachable via an explicit `data-theme="elvish"` selector, never via system preference (there's no `prefers-color-scheme: elvish`).

**L266–281**: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` zeroes all `--duration-*` and disables `::view-transition-*` animation — theme-invariant, applies identically under any `data-theme`.

**L284–297 `[data-theme="oracle"]`**: the precedent scoped-theme block — **does not touch any semantic token** (no `--surface-*`, `--ink`, `--accent` etc.). It declares 9 entirely new namespaced custom properties (`--oracle-bg`, `--oracle-bg-elevated`, `--oracle-fg`, `--oracle-fg-muted`, `--oracle-rule`, `--oracle-gold`, `--oracle-cream`, `--oracle-maroon`, `--oracle-marginalia-fg`) plus 3 font-family aliases (`--font-oracle-body/-display/-fraktur`). Oracle CSS modules consume `--oracle-*` directly, never `--surface-canvas` etc. **This is the key architectural fork elvish design must choose between**: (a) a full-app theme like light/dark, overriding the same ~30 semantic tokens so all ~11 surfaces styled purely with tokens repaint automatically, or (b) a scoped route-local palette like oracle, requiring every consuming component to be re-pointed at new `--elvish-*` vars. Given the brief says "third theme" (a room, not a route), **(a) is the correct model** — elvish must define full overrides on `[data-theme="elvish"]` for every token dark/light define.

**L299–402**: reset + body base (font/color/bg from tokens, `isolation: isolate` for grain stacking context L325), canvas grain pseudo-element (L328–337, `body::before`, opacity/image driven by the per-room knobs — elvish needs its own opacity/image choice, likely non-zero for a "living wood/leaf" texture or 0 for a clean parchment feel), link/button/input base rules, `.sr-only` (L362–372), global focus-visible ring using `--ring` (L374–377, theme-portable automatically), `::-webkit-scrollbar` track/thumb using `--surface-2`/`--edge`/`--ink-faint` (L380–396, theme-portable automatically), and a modal-scrim suspension rule (L397–402, unrelated to theming).

## 2. `apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx` (129 lines)

- `viewport.themeColor` (L36–39) is a **2-entry array keyed only on `prefers-color-scheme: light`/`dark`** — there is no cookie-driven `theme-color` meta at all today; it only reflects OS preference via `BRAND_BG_LIGHT`/`BRAND_BG_DARK` from `lib/brand`. An explicit elvish selection would leave the browser chrome/PWA titlebar colored per OS preference, not per elvish palette, unless this is extended (can't key `theme-color` media queries off cookies — would need a small client script or a fixed elvish `BRAND_BG_ELVISH` if the metadata API supported cookie-driven values, which it doesn't for static `<meta>`; likely acceptable to leave as-is or note as a known gap).
- 5 `next/font/local` declarations, each producing a CSS var via `variable:` and all concatenated onto `<html className>` (L122): `inter` (`--font-inter`, preloaded, body/LCP), `jetbrainsMono` (`--font-jetbrains-mono`, not preloaded), `ebGaramond` (`--font-eb-garamond`, normal+italic), `imFellEnglish` (`--font-im-fell`, normal+italic), `unifrakturMaguntia` (`--font-unifraktur`). **A new Tengwar-script font must follow the identical pattern**: local woff2 file(s) under `apps/web/src/app/fonts/`, a new `localFont({...variable: "--font-tengwar"})` call, and the variable appended to the `className` template string L122 (font vars load unconditionally on every route regardless of theme — cheap, `display:"swap"`, `preload:false` for non-Inter faces).
- `data-theme={theme ?? undefined}` (L121) — `theme` comes from `readThemeCookie()` (server-side, L117), typed `AppTheme | null` — **`undefined` (not "elvish") is what light/dark/no-selection currently distinguish; widening `AppTheme` is the single upstream type change** (see §3).
- No `color-scheme` CSS property or meta tag found anywhere in layout.tsx or globals.css — native form controls / scrollbar dark-mode auto-styling is NOT currently declared; not a blocker for elvish, just note there's no forced `color-scheme: light` to override for a light-family elvish variant if greens/golds skew light.
- `manifest.ts` (found separately) hardcodes `background_color`/`theme_color` to `BRAND_BG_DARK` unconditionally (not theme-aware) — irrelevant to elvish unless PWA install-badge color should also shift, out of scope for a 3rd-theme cutover.

## 3. Theme plumbing & type-widening surface

- **`apps/web/src/lib/theme/cookie.ts`** (9 lines): `export type AppTheme = "light" | "dark"`; `readThemeCookie()` reads `nx-theme` cookie, returns `null` unless value is exactly `"light"` or `"dark"` — **this is the literal gate that silently drops any other cookie value today**. Widening to `"light" | "dark" | "elvish"` here is required, plus updating the equality check (L7).
- **`apps/web/src/lib/theme/setAppearanceAction.ts`** (19 lines): server action `setAppearanceAction(value: AppTheme | "system")`; sets/deletes the `nx-theme` cookie 1:1. Only needs `AppTheme` widened (imports the type from cookie.ts) — no other change.
- **`SettingsAppearancePaneBody.tsx`** (77 lines, `apps/web/src/app/(authenticated)/settings/appearance/`): client component. Local `type Selection = "light" | "dark" | "system"` (L10) needs a 4th arm `"elvish"`. The cookie-read regex L16 `/(?:^|;\s*)nx-theme=(light|dark)/` is a **second literal gate that must be widened** or elvish selection will read back as "system" after reload. The render is 3 radio `<label>`s (L38–72) each with value/checked/onChange + a styled name ("Study"/"Press") and one-line hint; adding elvish is a 4th identical block with a new name (needs an in-fiction room name per the "Two Rooms"→three-rooms narrative) and hint copy. `handleChange` (L21–29) just toggles `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` directly (instant, no reload) then persists via the server action — this mechanism needs no change beyond the type widening.
- **Cookie name grep**: `nx-theme` appears in exactly 4 files — the 3 above plus nowhere else (confirmed via repo-wide grep; no middleware, no other readers).
- **Literal-union grep for "light"|"dark"`**: 4 files matched, but only `cookie.ts` and `SettingsAppearancePaneBody.tsx` are the app-theme type (both need widening, above). The other two are **unrelated, narrower theme concepts that should NOT be conflated with elvish**: `lib/reader/types.ts:14` `ReaderTheme = "light" | "dark"` (the in-document reader's own light/dark toggle, independent of app theme) and `components/ui/MachineText.tsx:34` `MachineDocumentTheme = "light" | "dark"` (machine-voice code/log rendering mode). Neither is wired to `nx-theme`; whether elvish should introduce a third reader-theme variant is a product decision, not a mechanical requirement — out of scope for "does the app theme system need touching."

## 4. Token discipline gate — `apps/web/scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs` (294 lines)

Run via `bun run lint:css-tokens` (`apps/web/package.json:10`); not explicitly seen wired into `scripts/test` or a `.github/workflows/*.yml` job by name in this pass (only `lint` and `test:eslint-policy` script entries were confirmed adjacent — treat `lint:css-tokens` as at minimum a local/pre-merge gate that will reject any elvish CSS violating it; grep `ci.yml` for `lint:css-tokens` before assuming it's CI-enforced).

Two enforcement passes over every `src/**/*.css`:
1. **Color-literal ban** (L8–9, `COLOR_LITERAL_PATTERN` = hex/rgb/rgba/hsl/hsla/oklch): forbidden everywhere except an explicit `allowedFiles` allowlist (L11–18: `globals.css`, `brand.css`, one media-page module, `textDocumentReader.module.css`) plus two path-prefix exemptions (L84–93): `src/app/(authenticated)/oracle/**` and `src/app/(authenticated)/atlas/**` — **the atlas exemption is the only precedent for a whole-directory raw-color carve-out with a documented "manuscript register" palette (`--atlas-*` edge tokens), i.e. elvish, if it needs any raw literals beyond globals.css, would need either a similar allowlisted directory or (preferably) stay 100% token-driven and need zero exemption**.
2. **Undefined-custom-property check** (L204–221): every `var(--foo)` reference must resolve to something declared somewhere in `src/**/*.css`, or be in `runtimeCustomPropertyOwners` (L48–78, JS-installed vars: 5 font vars from `layout.tsx` + 6 component-measured geometry vars), or carry an inline CSS fallback (`var(--foo, fallback)`, detected by `hasInlineFallback` L142–157). **Any new `--elvish-*` var declared only in a component file without a `globals.css`/allowed-file declaration will fail this check** — declare all elvish-only tokens (e.g. Tengwar rune-border assets, elvish-specific grain) inside `globals.css` under `[data-theme="elvish"]`, mirroring oracle's pattern, not scattered in component CSS.
3. A third pass (L223–254) checks the **packaged Android offline-reading CSS bundle** (`apps/android/app/src/main/assets/nexus-offline/assets/*.css`) for vars it references but doesn't declare in its own closure — irrelevant to elvish unless the offline reader is meant to support it (see §9; almost certainly out of scope, offline bundle pins dark only).

## 5. Ornament/effect surfaces

- **Scrollbar**: `globals.css:380–396`, token-driven (`--surface-2`, `--edge`, `--ink-faint`) — repaints automatically under `[data-theme="elvish"]` once tokens are set, no extra work.
- **`::selection`**: only 2 occurrences repo-wide, both **hardcoded, not tokenized**, both inside `components/ui/MachineText.tsx` (L77 `#e6d6bd`/`#1a1a1c`, L121 `#5b4930`/`#fff` — likely a light/dark pair for machine-voice text blocks embedded as inline `<style>` strings, hence invisible to the CSS-file token-discipline scan since it's a `.tsx` string literal, not a `.css` file). **Global `::selection` styling does not exist elsewhere** — browser default applies on all other surfaces; elvish gets no free selection-color moment unless one is added, and MachineText's two hardcoded pairs won't shift for elvish without a code change (out of scope for design-only phase, but a design-relevant fact: no unified selection color today).
- **Focus rings**: token-driven via `--ring` (`globals.css:374–377`), fully portable.
- **Canvas grain**: `--canvas-grain-opacity`/`--canvas-grain-image`, set per room (dark: SVG turbulence noise at 0.035 opacity; light: none). Elvish needs its own decision — a third grain texture (e.g., subtle vellum/leaf fiber) or a Tengwar-glyph-tiled watermark reusing the same `body::before` mechanism at `globals.css:328–337`.
- **View transitions**: `startViewTransition`/`viewTransition` referenced in ~18 files (list-row activation, pane navigation — `lib/ui/viewTransitions.ts` is the shared helper; `globals.css` only touches `::view-transition-*` for the reduced-motion override, L275–280) — these are geometry/opacity crossfades, not color-keyed, so theme-invariant and need no elvish-specific work.
- **Code blocks**: `components/ui/hljs-theme.css` — 100% token-driven (`--ink`, `--surface-2`, `--accent`, `--success`, `--warning`, `--ink-faint`, `--accent-hover`, `--info`, `--danger`, `--ink-muted`), zero raw colors. Repaints automatically for elvish.
- **Highlight inks**: `lib/highlights/colors.ts` only holds color→label strings; actual ink values are the theme-invariant `--highlight-yellow/green/blue/pink/purple` rgba tokens in `globals.css:133–137`, deliberately not overridden per theme (design intent: highlight colors stay recognizable across rooms). Elvish inherits these unchanged unless a deliberate exception is designed.

## 6. Raw-color leakage in `*.module.css`

Only **4 files** contain any raw hex/rgb/hsl literal at all (repo-wide `*.module.css` grep) — token discipline is in practice very well enforced, not just gated:
1. `src/app/(authenticated)/media/[id]/page.module.css` — 26 matches (explicitly allowlisted, L14 of the gate script)
2. `src/app/(authenticated)/atlas/atlas.module.css` — 7 matches (path-prefix exempted)
3. `src/app/(authenticated)/oracle/oracle.module.css` — 3 matches (path-prefix exempted)
4. `src/components/reader/textDocumentReader.module.css` — 1 match (explicitly allowlisted, L17)

**Every raw-color file is already an accounted-for exemption in the gate script** — there is no silent/undocumented leakage elsewhere. This means elvish, if built as a pure semantic-token theme (the recommended model, §1), will apply **uniformly across the entire app with zero missed surfaces** — the token discipline gate has already done the work of guaranteeing this.

## 7. Oracle theme anatomy (scoped-theme precedent)

- Mounted via `OracleThemeWrapper.tsx` (8 lines): a `<div data-theme="oracle" style={{display:"contents"}}>` wrapping children — presumably rendered by the oracle route's layout (not read in this pass, but the wrapper itself confirms the mechanism: **scoping is a DOM-subtree data-attribute, not a document-root swap** — oracle can coexist with the outer light/dark room since `[data-theme="light"]` on `<html>` and `[data-theme="oracle"]` on a nested `<div>` don't conflict, CSS attribute selectors match independently and the oracle block doesn't reference `--surface-*`/`--ink`/etc. at all).
- Oracle does **not** override any of the ~30 shared semantic tokens — confirmed by reading `globals.css:284–297` fully: only 9 `--oracle-*` tokens + 3 font aliases, no `--surface-canvas`/`--accent`/etc. redefinition. Oracle components must therefore consume `--oracle-*` directly in their CSS (would need to check `oracle.module.css` to confirm, not read here, but the raw-color allowlist entry for it plus zero shared-token references in the scoped block strongly implies oracle-specific styling doesn't lean on the shared token layer at all).
- 3 dedicated fonts (`ebGaramond`, `imFellEnglish`, `unifrakturMaguntia`) loaded unconditionally in `layout.tsx` regardless of route/theme (not lazy per-route) — same pattern a Tengwar font would follow.
- **This is the model for a scoped/route-local theme, explicitly NOT what elvish needs** (per the brief: "a third theme," i.e., a full-app room switchable from Settings → Appearance, parallel to light/dark, not a route-locked skin). Elvish should follow the **light/dark full-token-override model instead**, and use oracle only as evidence that non-standard font-family aliases and namespaced ornament tokens (e.g. `--elvish-rune-*` for Tengwar border assets) can coexist cleanly alongside the semantic layer without disturbing it.

## 8. Tests/gates that could break

- **`EntrySurfaces.browser.test.tsx`**: L367 `it.each(["dark", "light"] as const)` runs WCAG-contrast assertions (4.5:1 text, 3:1 focus ring) against `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` for each value. This array is **static and would not auto-include "elvish"** — no break, but also no coverage; if elvish is later built, this is the natural place to add a 3rd case, and its existence is a hard constraint on elvish accent/ink color choices (greens/golds must independently clear the same contrast floors against the elvish canvas — this is a real design constraint, not just a code one, given green-on-dark and gold-on-light are both harder contrast pairs than the current warm-neutral scheme).
- **`DossierDocumentFrame.browser.test.tsx:31`**: hardcodes `theme: "light"` in test setup/props — a component-local prop (likely `ReaderTheme`, not `AppTheme`), unaffected by an elvish app theme unless that component is also asked to render an elvish reader variant.
- **`EntrySurfaces.browser.test.tsx:165`**: `removeAttribute("data-theme")` in cleanup — theme-agnostic, no risk.
- No snapshot tests, no `android-visual` references to theme found in this pass (android-visual lane per memory drives a real WebView against a real device; it authenticates and screenshots specific panes — would only be affected if elvish were made default or the tested panes assert on theme-derived pixel colors, neither indicated).
- **`lint:css-tokens` gate (§4)** is the most likely hard-fail surface: any elvish CSS work must declare every custom property it references inside `globals.css` (or another allowlisted file) and must not introduce raw color literals in ordinary component CSS.

## 9. Android app

`apps/android` is a **WebView wrapper**, not a native-UI reimplementation — confirmed by `NexusWebView.kt`, `MainActivity.kt` all under `app/src/main/java/app/nexus/android/` clearly orchestrating a WebView pointed at the hosted web app (Google Sign-In controller for auth handoff, share-intent activity — all wrapper concerns, no native color/theme UI). `themes.xml` (4 lines) is trivial: `Theme.Nexus` parents `Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar` with zero overrides — the **native chrome (status bar, splash, app-switcher card) follows OS day/night, not the in-app `nx-theme` cookie**; the web content itself, once loaded, renders whatever `data-theme` the cookie carries exactly as the browser does. So: **yes, elvish flows to Android automatically once shipped to the web app** — no native Android work needed — but the native status-bar/splash chrome will NOT match elvish (it only ever matches OS light/dark), a small but real seam if device-level polish matters. The **packaged offline-reading bundle** (`offlineReading.module.css`, `offline-reading/index.html`) is a separate, disconformant case: `index.html:4` hardcodes `<html data-theme="dark">` — the offline shelf is pinned to the dark "Press" room unconditionally and would NOT pick up elvish even if selected in the live app; extending offline reading to elvish (or to user theme choice at all) is unbuilt and out of scope here, just documented as an existing hard-pin.

## Summary: what a future "make elvish real" build touches

1. `globals.css` — one new `[data-theme="elvish"]` block, full token override (~30 tokens) + a Tengwar-glyph or leaf-vein grain choice, mirroring the light block's structure exactly (§1).
2. `layout.tsx` — one new `localFont` call for a Tengwar face + append its variable to `className` (§2); optionally address the `theme-color` meta gap for elvish's own browser-chrome color (currently OS-only, §2).
3. `lib/theme/cookie.ts` — widen `AppTheme` union + equality check (§3).
4. `lib/theme/setAppearanceAction.ts` — no change beyond the imported type (§3).
5. `SettingsAppearancePaneBody.tsx` — widen `Selection`, widen the cookie-read regex, add a 4th radio option with elvish room-name copy (§3).
6. New Tengwar `.woff2` file(s) under `apps/web/src/app/fonts/` (must be sourced/obtained — design phase only, not fetched here).
7. Everything else (scrollbars, focus rings, code blocks, view transitions, ~all component CSS) **repaints for free** because raw-color leakage is already near-zero and rigorously gated (§6) — this is the single most reassuring fact in the survey: elvish will look coherent app-wide the moment the token block exists, with no component-by-component hunt required.
8. Known gaps that stay out of scope for a first cutover: offline-reading bundle pinned to dark (§9), Android native chrome follows OS not app theme (§9), `MachineText.tsx`'s two hardcoded `::selection` pairs (§5), reader-local `ReaderTheme`/`MachineDocumentTheme` unions are separate from app theme and untouched unless a reader-level elvish variant is explicitly wanted (§3).
